title: How Sweet the Melting Lay
description: How Sweet the Melting Lay in Tonic Solfa to AYLESBURY, doh is Ab: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: These words were printed without an author's name in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 919 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “Morning Prayer Meeting”, where the book credits them to the Sacred Lyrics.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Short Metre (6.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to AYLESBURY; any other Short Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: How sweet the melt-ing lay, Which breaks up-on the ear, When, at the hour of ris-ing day, Christ-ians u-nite in prayer!

lines: When, at the hour of rising day,
He listens to their humble sighs,
Once on the chilling mount did stay,
To rescue souls condemned to die,

licence: Public domain: anonymous words in print by 1853.
credits: Words anonymous, public domain, as printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion (1853); set to AYLESBURY by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
